english.title: Fail to comply with a direction to prevent human consumption of contaminated food
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed to comply with a direction, namely **(..SPECIFY DIRECTION..), given by

(A)_[a designating authority, namely **(..SPECIFY AUTHORITY..),]_
(B)_[the Food Standards Agency]_

under section 2 of the Food and Environment Protection Act 1985 in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF NON-COMPLIANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 2(4)(a) and 21(1) and (2) of the Food and Environment Protection Act 1985.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) If the designating authority or the Food Standards Agency does anything by virtue of section 2 of the Food and Environment Protection Act 1985 in consequence of the failure on the part of any person to comply with such a direction then, under section 2(5), the authority taking that action may recover from that person any expenses reasonably incurred by the authority under section 2.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
